cells.tense: Right now you can tell what deserves your attention before your reasons arrive, and you are keeping it.
cells.act: return the favour at its true size
cells.ask: Something someone gave you lately, return at its true size — not more, not less. Notice the exact size before you do.
cells.core:
You can tell what matters here before you can explain how you know. Lately you've been holding something that came out of a change — a way of doing things, a quiet, an arrangement — keeping it steady while your reasons catch up. That is what this looks like going well: not gripping, just keeping a true thing true while it settles. This is where that way of knowing stands.

It can feed the exchange around it. The favour you owe someone sits at a size you already sense; giving it back at that size, not padded and not short, is ordinary and it moves. Do one of those this week and keep it small. Paying it clears a line that was holding you still, and the thing you've been keeping gets lighter.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters and keep it steady.
cells.verb: holding what a change produced, steady and intact
cells.place: where you know what matters before you can say why

cells.tense: Soon — you'll be guarding what you've kept against a harm that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Once this week, go toward the thing pulling at you — the feeling you keep almost having — and look at it up close. Decide nothing yet.
cells.core:
You know what matters before the reasons show. That's a gift for holding what a change produced — keeping the good thing that came out of it, steady and undamaged. But where you're braced, that same way of knowing turns into defense against a harm that hasn't arrived. You see a future and build a wall against it. Holding a true thing was the point; protecting a false one is what's happening.

There is a pull under the wall — a feeling you keep almost having and setting down again. Go toward that once, without committing to it, and see what is actually there. You keep the power to hold; nothing gets torn down. You only look, and the wall stops standing between you and the thing it was supposed to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing against a forecast you wrote.
cells.verb: holding what a change produced, steady and intact

cells.tense: You already walked through a door that changed what you keep, and you're still standing before it.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Pick one concrete thing you'll do next, and when the first push comes against it, hold that heading anyway.
cells.core:
A change has already happened around you. Something ended, something got cleared, and what came out of that clearing — a way of doing things, a quiet, a new order — you can't quite hold yet. You can still tell what matters. It's just not being used to keep anything. Nothing gets noticed or let go of, and the present has nothing to stand on.

You don't need feeling to move toward a direction you once chose. Pick a heading — one real thing you'll do — and when the next push arrives, hold the heading anyway, once. It gives you something to do with what you can still tell, and the place that's starved comes back from the outside in.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters and you've stopped holding anything.
cells.verb: holding what a change produced, steady and intact
cells.place: where you know what matters before you can say why

cells.tense: Right now, you know what matters and arrange things around it without ever calling it by your name.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Next time you quietly arrange something for someone, let the arrangement do the work. Don't announce it. Then notice what you actually did.
cells.core:
Things run steady around you. You know what matters, you arrange accordingly, and if someone asked you to account for it, you'd say you weren't really involved. That is not false; it's the shape of hands doing good work while the eyes watch something else. You keep the thing that came out of the change standing — no heroics, just a quiet order that others arrange themselves around.

What returns it is the simpler form, done on purpose: let the arrangement act instead of announcing it, once. Then notice what you actually did. That last part is the whole act — you don't have to take credit, just to have seen it. The order stays; you stay with it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the order and say you're not involved.

attempts.check: Status 4's core says the person supplies a steadiness others organize themselves around; the record shows the capacity operating without their awareness, not that they deny it or that others lean on them. A reader could say, 'I never asked to be the ground everyone stands on,' which the cell should leave room for. The ask survives being wrong: someone who does not recognize themselves as the steady one can still do it and learn something. The line that serves the writer more than the person is any version of 'they trust the ground you forgot you were' — cut it, because it asks the person to accept a role they never chose.
